title.description: The record's headline. NOT A GUARDED MARK: it is the page's <h1>, not a mark a competing view could delegate away — if it fails to render there is no page. Covered observationally by tools/field-render-audit.mjs.

date.description: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD; use dateEnd for ranges. Bare YYYY is allowed because some records are known only to the year, and inventing a month would assert precision the source does not have.

term.description: baseline = pre-May-2014 (UPA era); T1 = 2014-19; T2 = 2019-24; T3 = 2024-. These values share their spelling with the source ladder's tiers BY ACCIDENT and are an unrelated axis: `term` T1 is a period of government, `sources[].tier` T1 is an evidence grade. A 2026-08-06 edit adding the source tier T1F to every `T1, T2` pair across these schemas landed here too; `tools/enum-parity.mjs` named it in the same run that named the intended change, which is the first thing that gate caught.

items.description:
The subject area a record belongs to. A TAG SET, not a partition: a ledger record carries `domains[]` and may carry several, a series carries exactly one, and a phase is not a domain — phase 7 produced eight records filed across seven values.

THE DISTINCTION THAT GETS CONFUSED IS welfare AGAINST human-development: welfare is the DELIVERY of a scheme, human-development is the OUTCOME it was meant to produce. Records carrying both (Swachh Bharat, PM-JAY, the anaemia reversal) are the normal case, not an error — the scheme is one domain and what it did to people is another. Education holds both the delivery and the outcome of schooling; it is not split across welfare and human-development the way a scheme is.
- macro: aggregate economic conditions and fiscal or monetary policy.
- banking: banks, credit, financial supervision and resolution.
- employment: work, labour force, earnings and formality.
- poverty: measured deprivation and consumption-based poverty.
- human-development: outcomes in health, nutrition and survival — what delivery produced.
- infrastructure: physical networks and their capacity or service.
- welfare: scheme delivery and entitlements — what was provided.
- education: schooling and higher education — learning, participation, teaching capacity and the education system.
- governance: institutions of state, enforcement, transparency and rights.
- kashmir: a cross-cutting lens, applied to records whose primary subject sits elsewhere.
- federalism: Centre-state relations. Also a lens: GST and groundwater carry it alongside their own subject.
- foreign: trade, external balances and relations with other states.
- defence: armed conflict and counter-insurgency operations, external or internal. The state’s treatment of civilians in those operations files governance, not defence.
- environment: land, water, air and the resource base.

lenses.description:
A cross-cutting LENS the record is also read under. `domain` says what the record IS ABOUT; `lenses[]` says what it ALSO BEARS ON. They are two axes, and a single-valued `domain` cannot hold both — every phase-11 series is substantively a defence or governance measurement AND is about Jammu and Kashmir, and while only the first was expressible a reader filtering the instrument on `kashmir` reached no measured spine at all. Optional; absent means no lens applies, which is the ordinary case. A lens is never a substitute for the subject: the substantive subject always goes in `domain`.
- kashmir: Jammu and Kashmir as place and question — the record's subject sits elsewhere (defence, governance, welfare) and J&K is the territory, population or conflict it is measured over. NEVER a subject value. The domain enum's own line reads "a cross-cutting lens, applied to records whose primary subject sits elsewhere", so `domain: "kashmir"` declares a lens and no subject at all, and is an error (rule `lens-as-subject`).
- federalism: Centre-state relations bearing on a record whose subject is elsewhere — GST as a macro record that moves fiscal authority between Centre and states, groundwater as an environment record on a state subject. UNLIKE kashmir this value is ALSO a subject in its own right ("Centre-state relations"), so `domain: "federalism"` is legal. What is not legal is asserting it on both axes of one record: either alone is correct, both at once says the record's subject is a lens over itself (rule `lens-duplicated`).

SIX VALUES ADDED IN PHASE 14, AND THEY ARE A DIFFERENT SHAPE FROM THE FIRST TWO. `kashmir` and `federalism` were derived FROM the domain enum, which had written both as lenses; these six are not domain values and never will be. A counterparty is not a subject area — "china" answers WHO a record is about, not WHAT it is about, and the subject of every one of them is trade, external balances or relations, which is `foreign`. The lens axis is therefore wider than the subset-of-domains relation it happened to have while it held only two values, and `lenses[]` being a subset of the domain enum was an accident of its first population, not a rule.
A LENS IS ADMITTED WHEN ITS RECORDS LAND, NOT WHEN IT IS PLANNED. `china`, `neighbourhood` and `europe` are named in the phase-14 plan and are deliberately NOT in the enum above: they enter with the records that populate them. A declared value with nothing behind it is a filter that returns nothing to the reader who selects it, which is the same defect as a lens with no page one level in — and the `lens-empty` gate refuses the build rather than trusting an author to notice.
A COUNTERPARTY LENS IS DECLARED ONLY WHERE THE INSTRUMENT HOLDS A FILE — several records read together because the counterparty is itself the policy object. It is not declared for a single agreement: a lens over one record is a filter that returns what a reader already had. UAE CEPA and Australia ECTA carry no counterparty lens for that reason, and the vocabulary extends when a file forms, not when a country is mentioned.
- defence-sector: the record's subject is the armed forces, the defence industry or defence procurement, whatever domain it files. DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED `defence`, because the domain of that name is narrower — "armed conflict and counter-insurgency operations" — and the lens is wider than it: an acquisition cost files `macro`, an indigenisation share files `foreign`, and neither is armed conflict. Two names for two different extents, so neither can be read as the other.
- united-states: the United States as counterparty — tariff actions, the negotiation track, visa and services measures, defence and technology frameworks.
- china: the People's Republic as counterparty — the merchandise deficit and its composition, import dependence and export controls, investment screening, and post-Galwan normalisation READ AS A DIPLOMATIC INSTRUMENT. The conflict itself is phase 11's and files `defence`; this lens is not a route to restating it.
- russia: the Russian Federation as counterparty — crude and refined-product flows, payment mechanisms, defence supply, and the linkage of any of them into a third country's measures.
- neighbourhood: the immediate South Asian neighbourhood as ONE object, which is why it is one value and not seven. The counterparty lenses above are each a file because each state is individually a policy object; here the region is the stated policy object — "Neighbourhood First" names a region, not a country — and the records are read as a set. A reader wanting one country reads the titles, and if a single neighbour accumulates a file of its own it earns its own value then. Pakistan is a member of the region and the member the doctrine least describes; its records are not yet authored.
- europe: the EU, the UK and EFTA as counterparties. One value, because the three are one negotiating arc in this instrument's material — an in-force UK agreement, an in-force EFTA agreement carrying an investment commitment, and a live EU negotiation — and splitting them would give each a filter with one record behind it.

type.description:
What KIND of thing the record is — not what domain it concerns and not how it turned out.
The distinction that gets confused is a measure the state chose against a disruption it did not: see the note on `shock`.
- reform: a measure the state deliberately introduced — a law, scheme, programme or rate change.
- event: a discrete dated occurrence, over in days or weeks.
- episode: a pattern or contested question observed over a span, with no single act at its centre.
- shock: a disruption arriving from outside the government's control.
- institutional: a change to the rules of the game or to a standing body, rather than a programme run through one.
SETTLED 2026-08-06 BY OPERATOR RULINGS 6 AND 7. This note previously read, and is quoted so the correction can be checked: "USAGE NOTE, unresolved: `shock` is currently applied both to external disruptions (the taper tantrum, COVID, US tariffs) and to domestically caused failures (the IL&FS collapse; the 2020 migrant exodus, whose own caseAgainst records that the four hours' notice 'was a choice'). The definition above states the external reading, which fits three of the five. The other two have not been reclassified." THAT COUNT WAS STALE IN BOTH ITS NUMBERS — there are EIGHT `type: shock` records, not five, and on the external reading four pass cleanly (L-0002, L-0021, L-0184, L-0186), two fail (L-0064, L-0216), one is mixed (L-0020, which bundles the contraction with the fiscal response) and one was unreachable by the test as then stated (L-0027). RULING 6: `shock` IS EXTERNAL TO THE STATE'S OWN DECISIONS. A chain of state decisions is not a shock however severe its consequences. The line is whether AN ACT OF POLICY CAUSED IT — not how severe it was (the 2020 migrant exodus was among the largest internal migrations in India's recent history and is a consequence of a decision) and not whose asset failed (the July 2012 grid collapse, L-0001, was a failure of state-OWNED infrastructure and no policy act). The test is L-0091's, which stated it before any rule existed: a record is not a shock where the thing recorded was "a sequence of state decisions rather than an external event". RULING 7: TYPE BY WHAT THE RECORD IS ABOUT, NOT BY WHAT FAILED. A record about the STATE'S RESPONSE to an event is typed by the response — L-0028 does this already and nothing told it to, being `episode` for the RBI moratorium and reconstruction scheme although Yes Bank's failure is a domestic non-state event. This is why no third branch for domestic non-state events is needed: the type turns on the SUBJECT OF THE RECORD and not on the nature of the event, which resolves IL&FS, the bank frauds of L-0032, the 2012 grid collapse and the 2022 heat shock without one. RETYPING ANY EXISTING RECORD IS VERDICT-ADJACENT AND IS NOT AUTHORISED BY THESE RULINGS; what moves is reported and the move is a separate deliberate act. APPLIED 2026-08-06 by operator instruction, as a separate deliberate act after the rulings were written: L-0216 to `reform` (the Cabinet Committee on Security’s own decision), L-0064 to `episode` (the exodus is the consequence of the lockdown notice its own caseAgainst calls a choice), L-0027 to `event` (the failure itself, not the state’s response to it). FIVE `type: shock` RECORDS REMAIN AND THEY ARE NOT THE FIVE THE STALE NOTE ABOVE MEANT: L-0002, L-0020, L-0021, L-0184, L-0186. Four pass the external reading. L-0020 IS THE OPEN CASE AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT RETYPED: it carries two subjects, which its own title states — an external contraction and a domestic fiscal response — and they take different types on any answer, so no retype settles it. A split into two records, or a decision about which subject the record is, is more than a retype; the question is written into that record’s own assessmentNote rather than resolved. No assessment moved in the retype and none may: a type change that would move a verdict is a stop. RULING 8 governs where a shock BELONGS — provenance, not the ledger — and is in CLAUDE.md with the two things it does not settle.

summary.description: What the record says, in one or two sentences. NOT A GUARDED MARK: body copy of the record's own page, with no competing view to delegate it to. Covered observationally by tools/field-render-audit.mjs. Distinct from `caveat`, which qualifies this and IS guarded, because a qualification is exactly what a dense view drops first.

claimAtLaunch.description: What the government said this would achieve, where applicable. NOT A GUARDED MARK: body copy rendered unconditionally in the record's own definition list. Covered observationally by tools/field-render-audit.mjs. A VOCABULARY FOR THE ABSENCE, 2026-08-06, on the `unmeasured[].reasonKind` model and designed WITH `objectives[]` because the two contradict otherwise. The field is EMPTY on 137 of 223 records and four different situations render identically: nothing was announced because the record is a condition or a pattern; something was announced and the record did not capture it; a statutory or constitutional benchmark applies (Ruling 5); or the field was simply not filled. WHERE NO CLAIM WAS MADE, WRITE ONE OF THESE AS THE FIRST TOKEN, THEN PROSE: `NONE ANNOUNCED` — the record is a condition, trend or pattern with no announcing act. `NONE LOCATED` — an announcing act exists and no statement of objective has been retrieved. THIS ASSERTS A SEARCH and carries the same stated-search obligation as `not-published`; where the search was not made, `NONE ANNOUNCED` is the weaker and safer value. `BENCHMARK` — the record is scored against a statute, a constitutional provision or a court direction under Ruling 5, named on the spot. THE FIELD IS NOT YET REQUIRED and the token is not yet enforced on records that lack it: making it required would break 137 records in one commit and the backfill is authoring, not migration. What IS enforced from 2026-08-06: a record whose `claimAtLaunch` opens `NONE ANNOUNCED` may not carry `objectives[]`, and a record carrying `objectives[]` must carry a `claimAtLaunch` or be a Ruling 5 imposed duty. That pairing is the contradiction the two were designed together to prevent.

objectives.description: THE OBJECTIVES A COMMITMENT ANNOUNCED, AS A LIST. Added 2026-08-06, and every property on it was required by a ruling or by a measured gap rather than anticipated. WHY IT EXISTS. Ruling 2 says an unmeasured limb prevents `worked` and Ruling 9 says a verdict resting on fewer objectives than were announced must say which ground it. NOTHING IN THE CORPUS RECORDED THAT A RECORD ANNOUNCED SEVERAL OBJECTIVES, so neither rule could be applied by a gate or re-applied by a reader: the phase-15 sweep that produced Ruling 2 counted EIGHT records stating multiple objectives IN THEIR OWN NOTES, and reading the 86 `claimAtLaunch` values found 43. A rule whose population is measured by self-narration cannot reach the records that did not narrate. SCOPE: records that announced something. Ruling 5's IMPOSED DUTIES BELONG HERE TOO — a duty in a statute, a constitutional provision or a court direction is an objective, so L-0095's Right to Education section 26 ceiling is an entry here with `grounds` true and no `claimAtLaunch` at all. NOT A SCORE AND NOT A CHECKLIST: the list records what was promised and which parts the verdict rests on. No count of objectives met rolls up anywhere, ever.

text.description: The objective in the announcement's own words, or the duty in the instrument's own words where it is imposed. Never paraphrased into a target.

quantified.description: Does the objective carry a number or a date that could be checked against an outturn? Ruling 9's second prohibition turns on this and it is not the same question as whether it was measured: AN UNMEASURED LIMB HAS A DENOMINATOR NOBODY PUBLISHED; AN UNQUANTIFIED LIMB HAS NONE AT ALL. L-0209 is the case — a fence of 1,643 km, quantified, and a paved patrol track whose length is stated nowhere — and only the second is a defect of the announcement rather than of the reporting.

measurement.description:
Whether this objective was measured, and what the measurement showed.
- met: measured, and the objective was achieved.
- not-met: MEASURED AND FAILED. Distinct from `unmeasured` and the distinction is load-bearing — 'a limb measured and failed and a limb never measured are different situations' is what decided Ruling 2, and L-0222 turns on it: both its limbs were dated, both fell due and both were missed, so `partly` was refused.
- unmeasured: nobody measured it. The absence belongs in `unmeasured[]` and `unmeasuredRef` points at it.
- unmeasurable-no-event: THE QUANTITY IS WELL DEFINED AND WOULD BE COLLECTABLE, AND THE EVENT WHOSE MEASUREMENT IT PRESUPPOSES DID NOT OCCUR. Added here rather than to `unmeasured[].reasonKind` because it is a property of the OBJECTIVE and not of a holder: `reasonKind`'s ladder asks whether the data exists and is asked OF A HOLDER, so `not-collected` would assert a failure to gather when the state's failure was elsewhere, and `never-defined` is simply false. L-0030 is the case — no public sector bank was transferred, so the efficiency of a privatised bank has no event to measure. IT MUST NOT BECOME AN EXCUSE: L-0030 is `failed` BECAUSE the transfer did not happen, and a record may not use this value to convert its own central finding into a measurement gap.

grounds.description: DOES THE VERDICT REST ON THIS OBJECTIVE? Ruling 9's core requirement, and the property that was INVISIBLE UNTIL THE RULE WAS WRITTEN — designing this field before the rule would have produced one that records measurement and not relevance. Where a verdict rests on fewer than all the announced objectives, the record names which ground it, which do not, and why, and every ungrounded objective is entered as an absence. FOUR RECORDS ALREADY DID THIS UNPROMPTED: L-0011 ('Four objectives were announced. Two are measured in this record and both fail'), L-0016, L-0041 and L-0030. `false` IS NOT A CRITICISM OF THE RECORD. A failure verdict resting on two decisive objectives of four is sound; what Ruling 9 requires is that a reader can see it is two of four.

commitmentState.description:
THE COMMITMENT STATE OF THIS OBJECTIVE. Per LIMB and not per record, because that is the corpus's own usage: L-0221 and L-0223 both file a limb as 'commitment state (a)' while the record carries a verdict. Building it as a record-level axis would have created an axis the corpus does not use.
- not-yet-due: a trigger date or condition is named and has not arrived.
- due-and-undelivered: the date passed, with evidence of non-delivery.
- abandoned: evidence of abandonment. ABSENCE OF NEWS IS NOT THIS, and no record currently carries it — what evidence of abandonment looks like is an open question the corpus has never had to answer.
- unfalsifiable: a total with no date, no phasing and no annual target. It has no trigger so it is not `not-yet-due`, can never fall due so it cannot reach `due-and-undelivered`, and absence does not evidence abandonment. SINCE RULING 3 THIS NO LONGER IMPLIES `no-objective`: L-0209 is `undated-commitment`, so the STATE and the VERDICT are two axes, which is why the state needed its own field.

unmeasuredRef.description: Index into this record's `unmeasured[]`, where an objective is `unmeasured` or `unmeasurable-no-event`. Closes the join a reader currently makes by hand: several records already enter the limb as an absence and nothing says THIS ABSENCE IS THE LIMB THAT THE VERDICT DOES NOT REST ON.

whatHappened.description: What actually happened, on the evidence retrieved. NOT A GUARDED MARK: body copy rendered unconditionally in the record's own definition list. Covered observationally by tools/field-render-audit.mjs.

assessment.description:
What the record concludes. These values had no written definitions until 2026-08-01, which is how `reversed` came to cover two different mechanisms without the type objecting. Definitions:
- worked: the measure achieved the objective stated at announcement, on the evidence available. TWO CONDITIONS, both ruled by the operator on 2026-08-06, and both of which make this the hardest value in the enum to reach.
  (1) INDEPENDENCE. The governing principle of this instrument is that NO RECORD OR CLAIM STANDS ON A SOURCE THAT IS NOT CREDIBLY INDEPENDENT OF WHAT IT ESTABLISHES. A press release from the party being assessed is not credible evidence that the party succeeded, however official the release and whatever tier the document earns — tier grades the ARTEFACT, this grades the RELATIONSHIP between the source and the claim, and they are different questions asked of the same citation. So `worked` requires at least one source independent of the announcing body. WHERE NO INDEPENDENT SOURCE EXISTS THE RECORD IS NOT `failed`: the outcome is UNESTABLISHED, not negative. Unestablished is `partly` where part of the objective is independently established, or `contested` where the readings genuinely diverge. Scoring an unevidenced success as a failure would be the same error pointed the other way, and the standard is about what the evidence can carry rather than about which direction the finding runs.
  (1a) THE INTRA-STATE TEST, ruled by the operator 2026-08-06 because (1) assumed two categories and the corpus has three. Intra-state evidence — one arm of the state measuring another — SATISFIES the principle where the measuring institution publishes the figure AS PART OF ITS OWN STATUTORY OR ROUTINE FUNCTION, and FAILS where the figure appears IN SUPPORT OF THE CLAIM. The RBI's Financial Stability Report qualifies; a joint ministry-and-regulator release does not. The test is on the PUBLICATION and not on the institution: the same body can produce a qualifying figure and a non-qualifying one on the same subject in the same month, and which it is turns on whether the document exists to report or to persuade. A CAG performance audit is the paradigm qualifying case; a PIB release carrying a regulator's number is the paradigm failing case, whoever computed the number, because the document IS the claim. Two conditions travel with it: the qualifying source must bear ON THE LIMB IN DISPUTE, and the qualifying document must be HELD — a Financial Stability Report reached only through a news site's account of it is T4 under the mirror rule and is not the document, so the test is not passed. Where a record rests on intra-state evidence the assessmentNote SAYS SO in those terms, because one arm of government measuring another is better than a department scoring itself and is not the same thing as independent evidence.
  (2) NO UNMEASURED LIMB. Where a commitment states several objectives and ANY ONE of them is unmeasured, `worked` is unavailable and the verdict is `partly`. This governs the class, not the records that exposed it. There is no centrepiece exception: a record whose own note explains why one limb should weigh less has DOCUMENTED a departure from this definition, not authorised one, and the method does not permit objectives to be weighted after the results are known.
- partly: the measure achieved part of its stated objective, or achieved it for part of the intended population.
- failed: the measure did not achieve the objective stated at announcement. Includes a measure struck down by a court, because the outcome is the same and only the mechanism differs — record the mechanism in assessmentNote. AN OBJECTIVE MAY BE IMPOSED AS WELL AS ANNOUNCED (Ruling 5, operator, 2026-08-06): a duty imposed by an EXTERNAL AUTHORITY — an authority other than the body being assessed, so a statute, a constitutional provision or a court direction — is a legitimate objective for scoring, PROVIDED THE RECORD NAMES THE INSTRUMENT, THE DUTY IN THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN WORDS AND THE DUTY-HOLDER. Four conditions, all required. (i) The obligation is IMPOSED, not volunteered, and the absence of a deadline in the instrument does NOT move it to no-objective — L-0162 and L-0210 are both stated, binary and undated and take failed and no-objective respectively, because Article 279A(11) binds the GST Council whether or not the Council ever said anything, while the Free Movement Regime position binds MHA only as far as MHA committed itself. (ii) The duty must be THE ONE THE FINDING IS ABOUT — L-0154's Article 281 duty was DISCHARGED and its finding is about five undefined action verbs no instrument reaches; this is Ruling 1a's bear-on-the-limb-in-dispute applied to an objective rather than to a source. (iii) NAMING AN INSTRUMENT IS NOT BREACHING IT — L-0122 names AFSPA (J&K) section 7, which sets no standard on the grant rate. (iv) AN ABSENT DUTY IS NOT A DUTY — L-0164's finding is that Articles 200 and 201 fix no period at all, which is the structural inverse. The rule does NOT reach an objective INTERNAL to the measure: L-0108 is failed against the recruitment process's own object and is scored under the ordinary definition above, and is named here so it is not cited as an instance and used to widen the rule by example.
- reversed: the ENACTING AUTHORITY withdrew or repealed its own measure. `measure` means an INTERVENTION THAT ACTS ON THE WORLD. Withdrawing a disclosure, a publication or a reporting practice is not reversal, even where the authority withdrawing it is the one that established it. Judicial invalidation is NOT reversed either: a court striking a measure down is not the enacting authority changing its mind, and collapsing the two loses the thing that distinguishes a government retreating under pressure from a government overruled. The value attracts anything that ends, which is why this line now states what a measure is and not only who withdrew it.
- contested: the evidence supports more than one defensible reading and the record does not choose between them.
- too-early: the measure is in force but has not run long enough for its stated objective to be testable. THE OBSTACLE IS ELAPSED TIME AND THE EVIDENCE TIME ACCUMULATES. Where the obstacle is instead a pending decision by a body outside the enacting authority, the value is awaiting-adjudication. Re-read against its two remaining members on 2026-08-03 and it describes both: L-0061, where outcome data has not yet accrued, and L-0139, the boundary case, where what is awaited is a year of post-commencement orders and any first setting-aside - things that accumulate with time rather than a ruling anyone is waiting on.
- awaiting-adjudication: the measure is in force and its effect is testable in principle, but the term that would settle the assessment is a pending decision by a body outside the enacting authority. Distinct from too-early, where the obstacle is elapsed time. Added 2026-08-03 after a sweep of all 149 ledger records found five records in this state and only six records carrying too-early at all - so 83 per cent of that value was occupied by a state its own definition did not describe. FOUR of the five take this value: L-0086, L-0127, L-0134 and L-0143. The fifth, L-0139, does NOT, because what it awaits is an act of publication by a holder rather than a decision by an adjudicator; the value is not stretched to absorb the member that contradicts its own definition.
- baseline-context: pre-2014 context, carried so that post-2014 records are read against a stated starting condition. Never scored; the schema ties it to term "baseline".
- no-objective: the record finds something real, and no objective was stated at announcement against which the finding could be scored. Distinct from contested, which is about the evidence supporting more than one reading. Use where nothing was claimed, not where a claim exists and its outcome is unmeasured — that remains contested (see L-0096). The value asserts nothing about the finding's quality: a no-objective record is as firmly established as any other, and the absence it records is the absence of a claim to test, not of evidence. Roughly half the ledger is in this state — conditions, trends, reporting instruments and structural absences — and before this value existed all of it had to take a value that presupposes an objective, which is why contested became a sink. AN IMPOSED DUTY IS NOT THE ABSENCE OF A CLAIM (Ruling 5, operator, 2026-08-06). This value reaches the case where nothing was claimed BY the government. It does NOT reach an obligation imposed ON the government by a statute, a constitutional provision or a court direction: where such a duty exists, is named in the record with its instrument and its duty-holder, and is the duty the finding is about, the record is scored against it — see failed. The absence of a deadline in the instrument does not restore no-objective, because Ruling 3's undated ladder governs what a government VOLUNTEERED and an imposed duty was not volunteered. Three things this value still correctly covers and that must not be confused with an imposed duty: a duty that was DISCHARGED while the finding is about something else (L-0154), an instrument NAMED but not breached (L-0122), and a finding that IS the absence of an obligation (L-0164).
- undated-commitment: a STATED AND QUANTIFIED commitment carrying NO DEADLINE, which therefore cannot fall due. Added 2026-08-06 on operator ruling, because `no-objective` was doing two contradictory jobs — nothing was claimed, and something concrete was claimed with no date attached to it. L-0209 is the case that forced it: a commitment to fence the entire 1,643-kilometre Indo-Myanmar border is a number a reader can hold, and classifying it as having no objective because an undated total cannot become overdue was true about the deadline and false about the claim. PROGRESS AGAINST SUCH A COMMITMENT IS REPORTABLE EVEN THOUGH IT CAN NEVER BECOME OVERDUE. The value says the CLOCK is missing, not the objective: a record carrying it should state how much of the stated quantity has been delivered and as of when, and its revisitTrigger should name what would move it. What it must not do is convert the absence of a deadline into the absence of a claim, which is what the previous classification did and which had the effect of insulating an undated promise from ever being scored at all. Distinct from `no-objective`, where nothing quantified was claimed; from `too-early`, where a deadline exists and has not arrived; and from `partly`, which presupposes a due date the commitment has no way of reaching.

independence.description:
THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE EVIDENCE AND THE CLAIM IT IS MADE TO CARRY. Added 2026-08-06. NOT THE TIER, AND THE TWO ARE ASKED OF THE SAME CITATION AND HAVE DIFFERENT ANSWERS: the ladder grades the ARTEFACT by its distance from the event, this grades the RELATIONSHIP. A ministry press release is a T1 document and, on the question of whether that ministry succeeded, no evidence at all; a CAG performance audit is T1 and is independent of the ministry it audits. WHY IT EXISTS. Independence is the axis five rulings turned on and the 6 August pass moved nine verdicts on it, AND IT WAS RECORDED NOWHERE: nine records state a finding in `assessmentNote`, in five distinguishable forms — a verdict on a named test, a labelled clause, a search narration, a degree statement, and one that never uses the word — and 212 state nothing of any kind. A pass that cannot be reproduced from the data is a pass that will drift.
- none: every source bearing on the claim is the announcing body or its own ministry. THIS IS A DESCRIPTION AND NOT A DEMERIT. L-0030 is the case: one authoritative statement that no public sector bank was privatised is not weak evidence, it is the right evidence, and `none` is correct rather than damning.
- intra-state: a different institution of the same state measured the announcing body, AND PUBLISHED THE FIGURE AS PART OF ITS OWN STATUTORY OR ROUTINE FUNCTION. Ruling 1a`s condition is part of the value rather than a flag beside it: the test is on the PUBLICATION and not the institution, so the RBI Financial Stability Report qualifies and a joint ministry-and-regulator release does not, whoever computed the number in it. Two further conditions travel with it and are not optional — the source must bear ON THE LIMB IN DISPUTE, and the document must be HELD, so a Financial Stability Report reached only through a news account of it is T4 under the mirror rule and the test is not passed.
- external: at least one source outside the Indian state bears on the claim.
ORDERED, AND THE ORDER IS EVIDENTIARY RATHER THAN MORAL: external > intra-state > none. NO VALUE FOR "not assessed", DELIBERATELY. That is what the absence of the field means, and a fourth value would let a record assert that it declined to look. WHERE THE RECORD`S OWN EVIDENCE DOES NOT SETTLE IT THE FIELD IS LEFT OFF and the count is reported, which is the honest state and not a gap. SCOPE: the evaluative class — worked, partly, failed, reversed. `failed` and `reversed` are IN scope and that asymmetry was argued rather than assumed: Ruling 1 raised the bar for agreeing with the government and said nothing about disagreeing with it, and a principle about what evidence can carry has no direction. A GUARDED MARK is not the right frame here — it is a non-prose value, covered by tools/field-render-audit.mjs through its label map, and rendered beside the sources rather than beside the verdict because it grades the evidence and a chip beside a verdict reads as a demerit.

contestedGround.description:
On a record scored `contested`, what would settle the contest. NOT a statement about confidence: it answers 'what would have to be true for this to resolve?', and for three of the six values the honest answer is nothing. Permitted only where assessment is `contested`.
- criterion: nothing would settle it. The facts are agreed and the dispute is which frame or objective governs.
- interpretation: an authoritative reading of a document or statute. None has been given, or two inconsistent ones have.
- evidence-withheld: a specific figure or document that exists or is producible, and is not published.
- measure: nothing would settle it, but the rival measures are enumerable - several valid published measures of one object point opposite ways and no party committed to one in advance.
- evidence-unobservable: nothing would settle it. The settling fact is a counterfactual, or is unbuildable while the practice stands.
- time: elapsed time. The readings make divergent predictions.
OPTIONAL WITHIN SCOPE, AND THE OMISSIONS ARE THE POINT. Two records - L-0092 and L-0129 - say in their own prose that `contested` is standing in for a value that does not exist. They are left UNVALUED rather than given an `other`, because minting a catch-all would absorb exactly the two records that are evidence this vocabulary is short, and the corpus would lose the signal that it needs extending. An absent value here means the ground has not been established or does not fit; it never means the question was not asked.
`disputeKind` DOES NOT TRANSFER AND THIS WAS TESTED. Its two values are defined against the stated reason for an ABSENCE - evidentiary means the holder's reason is contradicted by evidence the data exists, normative means the facts are agreed and the characterisation is contested. Neither has meaning applied to two readings of a measure. Forcing 23 records into those two boxes was proposed and withdrawn: the names transfer, the definitions do not.

caseFor.description: Strongest good-faith case in favour. NOT A GUARDED MARK: body copy, and it is structurally inseparable from the verdict — the schema already REQUIRES it on every scored record, so a missing case is a validation failure rather than a rendering one. Covered observationally by tools/field-render-audit.mjs.

caseAgainst.description: Strongest good-faith case against. NOT A GUARDED MARK: same reasoning as caseFor: required by the schema on every scored record, so its absence is caught before rendering is reached. Covered observationally by tools/field-render-audit.mjs.

event.description: The exogenous event, in prose. NOT a reference: no shock object exists, by Ruling 8 and its unsettled first item — see the field description. Name the event as the record names it.

role.description:
WHAT THE SHOCK DID to this record. Measured over all 66 prose values before the field was structured, and the two roles point OPPOSITE WAYS at a verdict, which is why one field could not carry both: `partly` on L-0017 (the shock may have caused the win) and `partly` on L-0090 (the shock degraded the measurement) meant different things and rendered identically.
- confound: the event degrades the measurement or makes attribution unclean. It debits nobody.
- cause: the event produced part of the outcome the verdict credits or debits. It moves the finding.
- is-the-shock: this record's own subject IS the event. Reflexive; there is no explanation to adjudicate, so `adjudication` is omitted.
- none-stated: the record states that no material exposure applies. A STATED ABSENCE IS A VALUE HERE AND NOT AN EMPTY FIELD — nine records wrote one unprompted ('None material', 'None external', 'None yet') before any rule asked them to, which is the opposite of `claimAtLaunch`, where 137 records are silently empty.

adjudication.description:
WHETHER THE RECORD ACCEPTS THE EXPLANATION. Orthogonal to `role`, and it is a modifier rather than a third role: 15 of the 66 prose values limited or refused the shock and only 4 did so as the whole of what the field said.
- accepted: the record accepts the event as stated (L-0054, 'accounts for a substantial share of route discontinuation').
- limited: accepted in part and bounded (L-0037, 'explains part but not all of the slippage').
- refused: named and rejected (L-0067, 'Neither explains the shortfall in the pre-2020 years').
- unstated: THE RECORD MADE NO ADJUDICATION. Authorised by the operator 2026-08-06 as a fourth value, and its definition is the point: it records that NO JUDGEMENT WAS MADE, not that the explanation is unresolved or pending. L-0209's neighbour L-0061 is the case — 'COVID intervened between passage and implementation and IS THE STATED REASON for much of the delay' names an explanation offered by someone else and never says whether the record accepts it. Each of the other three would assert a judgement the record declined, and FILING AN UNMADE JUDGEMENT UNDER A MADE ONE is the defect this cycle has spent itself correcting. Not a catch-all: a record that HAS adjudicated and is merely tentative takes `limited`.

why.description: The record's own reasoning, VERBATIM from the prose this field carried before 2026-08-06. A GUARDED MARK: it is the judgement, and a dense view that dropped it would leave a role and an adjudication with no ground.

shockExposure.description: What this record says about its own relationship to an exogenous event. ONE ENTRY PER EVENT-AND-ROLE. STRUCTURED 2026-08-06 (phase 16). It was a single prose string on 66 records, doing two jobs at once with opposite consequences for a verdict and read by nothing but its own page: no index, no filter, no cross-tab, no gate. THE PROSE IS THE ASSET AND SURVIVES VERBATIM in `why` on every entry — the judgement is there, and a field that replaced it with an identifier would destroy the thing being calibrated. WHAT THIS FIELD DOES NOT HOLD, AND THE CONDITION THAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT: the EVENT's own properties — its window, whether it is shared with the peer panel or India-specific, and whether it breaks a series. Those are facts about the event and not about any record, and restating them per record is the duplication this field exists to remove (L-0021, L-0184 and L-0186 assert nettability three times, two one way and one the other). They need a first-class shock object, and operator Ruling 8 puts that object in PROVENANCE — where `bridgeExists` asks whether there is an accepted reconciliation ACROSS THE BREAK and has no referent for a shock that breaks no series. SO THE EVENT STAYS PROSE, IN `event`, UNTIL A SHOCK BREAKS A SERIES. That is the condition, stated here so a later cycle knows what would unblock it rather than rediscovering the block: when a shock that breaks a series arrives, it takes a provenance record, `event` can become a reference to it, and the three properties land there and not here. None of the five `type: shock` records at the time of writing breaks a series.

items.description: Series id whose points this record is read against.
Provenance record id (P-nn) whose measurement dispute bears on this record.

tier.description:
Evidence grade of the DOCUMENT ACTUALLY RETRIEVED, not of the institution the subject belongs to. This is the operative rule and the one that goes wrong: a CAG finding known only through a newspaper's account of an RTI reply is T4, because the subject is official but the evidence is relayed. Grade what you hold, not what it is about. THE MIRROR RULE, ruled by the operator 2026-08-06: GRADE THE DOCUMENT, NOT THE SERVER. Identical bytes ARE the document — a judgment retrieved from a mirror, or a ministry PDF retrieved from the Internet Archive, is the document and keeps the tier the document earns. An ACCOUNT of a document is T4 — a newspaper reporting what a report said is journalism however official the subject. The distinction is between holding the artefact and holding somebody's description of it, not between which server sent the bytes. Two authoring requirements follow: RECORD THE RETRIEVAL PATH with the citation, so a reader knows the bytes came by a third party; and WHERE THE ORIGINAL NO LONGER RESOLVES, RECORD THAT BESIDE IT, because a publisher's deletion is evidence about the publisher and not about the evidence. This was decided on a measurement: of 17 archived primaries tested, 2 still answered at their original host. For 13 of 17 the archived copy is the only surviving copy, so grading mirrors down would have told a reader the evidence is weak when the publisher had deleted it.
- T1: official Indian statistical or institutional source, retrieved directly - a ministry release, an RBI, MoSPI or NCRB publication, a CAG report, a Parliamentary reply.
- T1F: a NON-INDIAN NATIONAL GOVERNMENT primary, retrieved directly - a foreign executive order, statute, court judgment, trade-representative determination or official gazette. Added 2026-08-06 on operator ruling. T1 is Indian official and T2 is multilateral; a foreign national government is neither, and 19 citations sat in T1 by default because the ladder had nowhere else to put them. A LETTER RATHER THAN A NUMBER, because the ladder's numbers descend in evidentiary strength and a US Federal Register notice is not weaker evidence than a contested composite index: T1F is T1's grade of artefact issued by a different state. It is its own tier because whose government published a document is information a reader of an instrument about the Indian government needs on the face of the citation. It also does work the ladder could not do before: under the independence principle governing `worked`, a foreign government primary IS independent of the Indian body being assessed and an Indian official release is not, and collapsing the two into one tier hid exactly that distinction.
- T2: multilateral or international statistical source, retrieved directly - World Bank, IMF, ILO, WHO.
- T3: peer-reviewed research or a working paper.
- T4: reported or documentary journalism, NGO datasets, and anything RELAYED rather than retrieved - including an official figure known only through a press account, and an RTI reply cited but not obtained.
- T5: contested composite index. Always carries a dispute record covering its own domain (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
Note that tier is asserted in exactly one place per layer: on the series itself, or on each entry of a ledger or provenance `sources[]`. A series `source` is a SourceRef and carries NO tier - the object is closed, so a tier inside it is rejected rather than silently ignored.

sources.description: Where every figure in this record comes from. NOT A GUARDED MARK: the source list is structural and is separately gated by url-check (every URL resolves) and no-bare-root (no citation may be a bare domain), which are stronger assertions than reachability makes. Covered observationally by tools/field-render-audit.mjs.

confidence.description:
How firmly the record's FINDING is established. Distinct from `tier`, which grades the evidence retrieved: a record can rest on a single relayed source and still be high-confidence if what it asserts is not in doubt, and can rest on a primary source and be medium if the reading is contested.
- high: the finding is well established and would survive a hostile reading.
- medium: the finding holds but rests on incomplete retrieval or a contested reading.
- low: the finding is provisional and should not be leaned on.
USAGE NOTE, unresolved: the field is ambiguous in practice between confidence in the FINDING and how well RETRIEVED the record is. L-0014 is high on a single T4 source while L-0015 is medium on a T1, which fits the finding reading; L-0089's revisitTrigger ties confidence to retrieving two primary documents, which fits the retrieval reading. The distribution is also heavily skewed — 63 high, 24 medium, 2 low across 89 records — so `low` is close to unattested. Nothing has been reclassified.

asOf.description: Date this record was last researched/updated

caveat.description: A blocking qualification that MUST render wherever this record appears, including compact listings. Use only when the record would mislead without it — an unverified comparability assumption, a circular measure, a disputed instrument. Not for ordinary uncertainty, which belongs in notes. Authored forms range from a short headline flag ("T5 CONTESTED INDEX") to a full sentence; the floor exists to stop an empty stub, not to require prose.

unmeasured.description: Dimensions this record SHOULD have but which have no measurement. An absence is a research finding, not an empty cell — declaring it here keeps it visible in every view rather than only where a component happens to supply it. Use when a chain has a missing link, an intended outcome was never measured, or a series stops short of the thing it is cited to demonstrate.

what.description: The thing that is not measured, stated positively

why.description: Why no figure exists — not collected, not published, withheld, or never defined

wouldFill.description: The source that would close it, if one is identifiable. Doubles as a verification-queue seed.

reasonKind.description:
The STATED reason no figure exists — what the responsible body says, not what is true. Where the stated reason is contradicted, set reasonDisputed and carry the contradiction in `why`.

THE TEST IS WHETHER THE DATA EXISTS, asked in this order:
- not-collected: never gathered. No record exists to release. If the holder were compelled tomorrow they would have nothing to produce.
- not-published: exists in a holder's hands, not released. The test is producibility under compulsion, not whether anyone has asked.
- withheld: exists, release was specifically requested or legally required, and was refused. Narrower than not-published — requires an identifiable refusal, not merely absence of release.
- never-defined: no agreed definition exists for the quantity, so it could not be collected even in principle. NOT "nobody has studied it" — an unstudied but definable quantity is not-collected.

reasonDisputed.description: True where the stated reason is contradicted by evidence — for example a body saying data was never maintained while another arm of the same government publishes some of it. The contradiction must be stated in `why`. This is not a fifth reasonKind: it is a dispute about which kind applies.

disputeKind.description:
What kind of contradiction reasonDisputed records. Required when reasonDisputed is true.
- evidentiary: the stated reason is contradicted by evidence that the data exists or was held.
- normative: the factual claim is not contested; what is contested is the characterisation of the non-release, typically against a legal or judicial obligation.

differentFacts.description: True where the two sides of the record do not share a common measure. Three conditions, of which the third is operative: (a) PRECONDITION — caseFor and caseAgainst cite different underlying quantities, measures or events, not the same one weighted differently. (b) PRECONDITION — neither case contradicts the other's factual claim, so granting one side's strongest fact in full leaves the other's case intact. (c) OPERATIVE — no single measure exists, or could be constructed from available data, that places both sides' facts on one ledger. An UNBUILT comparison FAILS (c): if a common denominator exists in principle and merely has not been built, that is a gap in the instrument, not a property of the argument. A counterpart that is DECLARED UNMEASURABLE passes (c). In practice (c) admits only arguments that cross a category boundary — a quantity against a legal ruling, a constitutional process, or a stated absence. Two economic cases almost always share a ledger in principle: an incidence analysis, a disposition table, a water-productivity account. The worked negative is the implicit taxation of farmers, where the OECD Producer Support Estimate nets budgetary support against implicit price transfers by construction.

differentFactsNote.description: What each side is counting, and why both can be arithmetically correct. Required in practice wherever differentFacts is true, and PERMITTED AND MEANINGFUL ON FALSE — a note on a false flag records why the record is a weighting case rather than a different-facts one, which is the judgement most at risk of being made silently. L-0118 is the worked instance: both sides accept every underlying fact, the temptation is to mark it true, and the note says so. Reading this line as true-only was a real misreading: it made the one deliberate false-note in the corpus look like a stray.

assessmentNote.description: WHY THIS VERDICT — the reasoning the verdict rests on, which is how the record page labels it and how the corpus uses it. CORRECTED 2026-08-06, and the previous description is quoted so the correction can be checked: it read "A note on the assessment VALUE itself — typically that the existing vocabulary does not cleanly fit and the value may change on review. Not a note on the finding, which belongs in caseFor/caseAgainst." THAT DESCRIBED A MINORITY USE AS THE WHOLE OF THE FIELD. Measured over the 171 records carrying one: 136 carry verdict-reasoning language and 6 carry vocabulary-fit language. The opening clauses settle it — "Assessed failed on the written definition", "Filed too-early because", "this record previously carried a verdict with no stated reasoning". THE VIEW WAS RIGHT AND THE SCHEMA WAS STALE, which is the inverse of the usual direction and is why it was measured before it was changed. The vocabulary-fit use survives and is not withdrawn: where a value does not cleanly fit, saying so here is still correct, and L-0092 and L-0129 are the standing cases. A GUARDED MARK, and the field the verdict chip links to. IT IS NOT REQUIRED AND 41 SCORED RECORDS CARRY NONE — 23 contested, 17 no-objective, 1 too-early — which is authoring work rather than a schema question: those verdicts stand without stated ground, which is the one thing this instrument says a scored record may not do.

revisitTrigger.description: A stated condition under which this record should be re-tested. Used where a judgement is correct now but rests on something that will change — most often a common measure that cannot yet be built but will become buildable. Distinct from assessmentNote, which is about the assessment VALUE rather than about when to look again.
